text: "residential district" shall mean any district described as Village Residential - VR, Residential R-1, Residential R-2, Residential R-4, Residential R-6, Residential R-10, Residential R-15, Neighborhood Model - NMD, Planned Unit Development - PUD or Planned Residential Development - PRD on the official zoning map of the county.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. Script: scratchpad scripts/proc.py. Parcel-based zoning polygons dissolved; morphological closing of 12 m (buffer +12 m / -12 m) to fill street rights-of-way between zoned parcels inside a district; holes < 2000 m2 and parts < 200 m2 dropped; tolerance 0.0001 deg.
notes: Result 82.6 km2 = 4.4% of the county. Codes map one-to-one to the ordinance list. The layer is parcel-based, so public road rights-of-way are not zoned in the data; the 12 m closing fills most interior streets but wide highway ROW at district edges may show small gaps (discharge on/across roads is separately unlawful under state law). Town of Scottsville (own zoning) and Downtown Crozet District, Monticello Historic District and commercial/industrial districts are not on the ordinance's list and were excluded. The City of Charlottesville is a separate jurisdiction (hole in the county) and is not covered.

text: in the northern part of the city beginning at the Chesapeake/Virginia Beach city line at its intersection with Centerville Turnpike, continuing on Centerville Turnpike in a southerly direction to its intersection with Mount Pleasant Road, continuing on Mount Pleasant Road in a westerly direction to its intersection with the railroad tracks, continuing along the railroad tracks extending northward to its intersection with the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway, continuing along the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway extending westward to its intersection with the Southern Branch of the Elizabeth River, continuing westward to its intersection with Interstate Route 64 and continuing along such road to its intersection with Interstate Route 664, continuing to its intersection with the Suffolk city line
method: constructed from TIGER
notes: Line used: Centerville Tpk from the Virginia Beach line south to Mount Pleasant Rd; Mount Pleasant Rd west to the Norfolk Southern track; the track north to the Albemarle & Chesapeake Canal (AIWW, -76.2101,36.7222); the AIWW westward through Great Bridge to its junction with the Southern Branch main stem, then down the Southern Branch to the I-64 High Rise Bridge (-76.2993,36.7582); I-64 west to the Bowers Hill interchange; I-664 north to the Suffolk line. Area kept = the part of the city north of that line. Doubts: (1) 'continuing to its intersection with the Suffolk city line' after I-664 was read as following I-664 north to where it leaves the city; the alternative reading (straight from Bowers Hill west to the Suffolk line) would add the narrow strip of Chesapeake west of I-664 (Bowers Hill / Hodges Ferry edge) - treat that strip with caution. (2) 'continuing westward' from the AIWW/Southern Branch junction to I-64 was followed down the Southern Branch (which runs north there), not along Deep Creek. (3) The app's city outline is the generalized Census 1:500k boundary, so the northern city edge against Norfolk/Portsmouth is coarse and some real city land is missing at the edges. Within the area, only pellet shotguns on 50+ acre agricultural/conservation tracts with a police permit are allowed (plus the deer exceptions in (f)/(g)).

text: in the area of the county bordered to the north by the James River, to the west by Route 602 from the Willis River, and to the south by Route 45 and Route 684 to the county line
method: constructed from TIGER
notes: Interpreted as the small Cartersville-area wedge in the NE corner: Route 602 from its crossing of the Willis River (-78.1136,37.6854) south to Route 45 (-78.1188,37.6603); Route 45 east to Route 684 (-78.0998,37.6580); Route 684 southeast to the Powhatan County line (-78.0841,37.6472); county line north to the James; the James River upstream (west) to the mouth of the Willis River, and the Willis River briefly back up to the Route 602 crossing. This is the only reading in which all named features close a polygon. Alternative reading not mapped: the lobe east of the northern part of Route 602 (north of the Willis River, up to the James) - 602 does not reach the James there, so it cannot close on its own. The app's county outline is generalized (Census 1:500k) and cuts inside the true James River bank, so a thin strip of real land along the river is missing. The ordinance's other area - all public lands in the county - is not part of this polygon. Rule: no deer hunting in the regular season with rifles .23 cal or larger unless from a tree stand at least 10 ft high.

text: It shall be unlawful to shoot or discharge any firearm, compound bow, cross-bow, air-operated weapon or gas-operated weapon in the following high density areas of the county, except for the protection of one's life or property: (1) R-2 Limited Residential. (2) Gwynnfield Subdivision. (3) Maryfield Subdivision. (4) Daingerfield Subdivision. (5) Shellfield Beach. (6) Richmond Beach. (7) Riverdale. (8) Tuscorora. (9) South Hill Banks. (10) River Oaks. (11) Fort Lowery Beach. (12) Grandview Subdivision. (13) Millers Square. (14) Wilson Acres. (15) Rappahannock Beach. (16) Kaighn Subdivision. (17) Old Howetons Road Subdivision.
method: Downloaded all 10,255 Essex County tax parcels (county ArcGIS Online layer, LegalDescr + TaxMap fields). Matched each name against the assessor legal description (excluding "ADJ ..." = adjacent-to parcels), then used the tax-map page/block that the matches fall on (Essex tax-map pages are drawn per subdivision, e.g. 26C = Gwynnfield) to take every parcel on that page/block. Unioned parcels, morphological closing of 25 m to absorb internal roads, filled holes < 2 ha (not clipped to the coarse county outline, since waterfront lots extend past it), simplified 0.0001 deg, rounded to 5 decimals. R-2 zoning item (1) is out of scope here.
notes: Parcel-derived approximations of subdivision extents (no official subdivision boundary layer exists). Per-name caveats: Richmond Beach: Only 2 parcels carry the RICHMOND BEACH legal description (lots 14-16, tax map 37C block 1). Polygon = all 9 parcels of tax map 37C block 1 (Richmond Beach Rd / Granary Rd). Lies 100% inside the Census place boundary of the Town of Tappahannock; whether the county ordinance applies inside the town was not verified. Low confidence on extent. | Riverdale: Two assessor groups use the RIVERDALE legal description: the main subdivision (tax map 37A blocks 1-3, sections A-C, ~70 lots, Rappahannock River south of Tappahannock) and a small 8-lot group on Summer Breeze Ln (tax map 47B block 1, near Tuscarora). Both are included; the 47B group is uncertain. | Tuscorora: Ordinance says "Tuscorora"; mapped as Tuscorora/Tuscarora Beach (incl. Tuscarora Beach II and the C B Allen plat parcels on tax map 47A). Nearby "Tuscarora Bray 1809" family divisions / Tuscarora Creek Estates / Tuscarora Pines were NOT included. | Shellfield Beach: Includes Upper Shellfield Beach (tax map 38 block 4) as well as Shellfield Beach (38D block 1); excludes Shellfield Landing (separate subdivision). | Old Howetons Road Subdivision: Ordinance spelling "Old Howetons Road"; matched to assessor legal description OLD HOWERTON ROAD lots 1-9 (tax map 44 block 7). | Fort Lowery Beach: Assessor spells FORT/FT LOWERY or LOWRY BEACH; tax map 38C blocks 1-2 (also contains Point Lowery Beach lots 1&2). | Daingerfield Subdivision: Tax map 31D block 1; excludes unrelated Wakefield lots on Daingerfield St (Tappahannock). | Kaighn Subdivision: Tax map 53A block 1 (Cottage Row); neighbouring Neale lots (53A block 2) excluded. | Millers Square: Tax map 49C block 1 (also contains 2 Perry's Place lots). | Gwynnfield Subdivision: Tax map 26C blocks 1-12 plus GWYNNFIELD (PART) boat landing & marsh parcel on map 26. Large lots; polygon spans ~375 ha. Parcel geometries are flagged by the county as being mid-update. Highest uncertainty: Richmond Beach, Riverdale (second group), Tuscorora.

text: It shall be unlawful to shoot or discharge any firearm, compound bow, cross-bow, air-operated weapon or gas-operated weapon in the following high density areas of the county, except for the protection of one's life or property: (1) R-2 Limited Residential.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. Script: scratchpad scripts/proc.py. District polygons dissolved; parts < 50 m2 dropped; tolerance 0.0001 deg.
notes: Result 7.1 km2 = 1.0% of the county. The ordinance (2012) says 'R-2 Limited Residential'; the current county zoning ordinance (adopted 10-11-2022) and the GIS layer name R-2 'Residential, Low Density'. I assumed this is the same R-2 district carried forward; I could not confirm a 'Limited Residential' label anywhere in current county material. Town of Tappahannock R2 is a different (town) district and was excluded. About 210 of the layer's ~1,970 R-2 acres fall outside the Census shoreline (riverfront lots extending into the Rappahannock) and were clipped off. The named subdivisions in the same section are a separate area (essex-county--named-subdivisions).

text: Firearms may lawfully be discharged in those areas that are exempted in Appendix J to the Fairfax County Code so long as the firearms are discharged on a Parcel of Land that is posted with signs giving reasonable notice that firearms are in use on that Parcel of Land and that no trespassing is allowed. ... Except for those persons who are on a Parcel of Land that is exempted in Appendix J and who hunt with shotguns loaded with multiple ball shot, it shall be unlawful for any person to hunt with a firearm which has a barrel caliber larger than a nominal 0.224 inches ...
method: No official vector layer for Appendix J was found (searched ArcGIS Online, Fairfax County ArcGIS org services1.arcgis.com/ioennV6PpG5Xodq0, and www.fairfaxcounty.gov/mercator). The text of Appendix J itself could not be retrieved (Municode blocked). Built from the county's official Appendix J "No Shooting Areas" map PDF: rendered at 300 dpi, pink (restricted) and yellow (exempt) fills classified by color, raster georeferenced to the county outline in VA State Plane North (4-parameter similarity fit, median residual ~2.8 px ≈ 170 ft), vectorized; the yellow/pink dividing line was then snapped to TIGER 2023 centerlines of the roads labelled on the map wherever the traced line lay within 250 ft of them (~89% of its length): Leesburg Pike (SR 7), Towlston Road, Sully Road (SR 28), Braddock Road (SR 620), Ox Road (SR 123), Silverbrook Road (SR 600), Lorton Rd connector, Richmond Highway (US 1). Non-road portions (Towlston Rd/Georgetown Pike to the Potomac near Difficult Run; Accotink Creek, Accotink Bay and the east shore of Gunston Cove around Fort Belvoir) keep the traced map line. The county was split by this line and each face assigned to restricted/exempt by majority overlap with the traced map fills.
notes: Exempt area = yellow "Areas exempted from prohibition on shooting firearms and pneumatic guns; however, shooting is subject to restrictions in Fairfax County Code Chapter 6" on the official map: Great Falls/Dranesville area north of Leesburg Pike and Towlston Rd; the strip west of Sully Rd; Centreville/Clifton/Fairfax Station south of Braddock Rd and west of Ox Rd/Silverbrook Rd; Lorton/Mason Neck south of Richmond Hwy and west of Accotink Bay/Gunston Cove. Share of county: 33.9%. Exempt does NOT mean shooting is generally allowed — it is only legal on posted qualifying parcels. Firearm discharge in the exempt area is still subject to Chapter 6: only on a "Parcel of Land" (per §6-1-1; the county wildlife page says 20 acres or larger) posted with signs; no hunting within 100 yards of primary/secondary highways; no slugs; .22-caliber limit except shotguns with multiple ball shot on exempt parcels; no shooting in/within 100 yards of public schools/parks. Accuracy: road-following segments use TIGER centerlines (±~10-20 m); non-road segments are traced from a letter-size county map (±~50-100 m). Towns of Herndon, Vienna and Clifton are colored on the map like their surroundings and are included (towns have their own ordinances). Cities of Fairfax and Falls Church are excluded by the jurisdiction outline. The map is dated November 2018; check for later amendments to Appendix J.

text: It shall be unlawful for any person to shoot any firearm in any areas of the County that are so heavily populated as to make such conduct dangerous to the inhabitants thereof, which areas are designated in Appendix J to the Fairfax County Code.
method: No official vector layer for Appendix J was found (searched ArcGIS Online, Fairfax County ArcGIS org services1.arcgis.com/ioennV6PpG5Xodq0, and www.fairfaxcounty.gov/mercator). The text of Appendix J itself could not be retrieved (Municode blocked). Built from the county's official Appendix J "No Shooting Areas" map PDF: rendered at 300 dpi, pink (restricted) and yellow (exempt) fills classified by color, raster georeferenced to the county outline in VA State Plane North (4-parameter similarity fit, median residual ~2.8 px ≈ 170 ft), vectorized; the yellow/pink dividing line was then snapped to TIGER 2023 centerlines of the roads labelled on the map wherever the traced line lay within 250 ft of them (~89% of its length): Leesburg Pike (SR 7), Towlston Road, Sully Road (SR 28), Braddock Road (SR 620), Ox Road (SR 123), Silverbrook Road (SR 600), Lorton Rd connector, Richmond Highway (US 1). notes: Restricted area = pink "Areas where firearms and pneumatic guns may not be shot except as otherwise provided in Fairfax County Code Chapter 6" on the official map; roughly everything east of Sully Rd and south/west of Leesburg Pike, Towlston Rd, Braddock Rd, Ox Rd, Silverbrook Rd and Richmond Hwy, including Fort Belvoir main post. Share of county: 66.1%. Firearm discharge in the exempt area is still subject to Chapter 6: only on a "Parcel of Land" (per §6-1-1; the county wildlife page says 20 acres or larger) posted with signs; no hunting within 100 yards of primary/secondary highways; no slugs; .22-caliber limit except shotguns with multiple ball shot on exempt parcels; no shooting in/within 100 yards of public schools/parks. Towns of Herndon, Vienna and Clifton are colored on the map like their surroundings and are included (towns have their own ordinances). Cities of Fairfax and Falls Church are excluded by the jurisdiction outline. The map is dated November 2018; check for later amendments to Appendix J.

text: that portion of the City south of Armory Drive and Second Avenue
method: constructed from TIGER
notes: Dividing line = Armory Dr from its west end (-76.9578,36.6663) east to W 2nd Ave, then W/E 2nd Ave northeast to its end near the Blackwater River (-76.9185,36.6806); both ends extended straight along the road bearing to the city outline (gaps of only ~40-70 m in the app's outline). Area kept = the part of the city south(-east) of that line, including downtown south of 2nd Ave. Firearm discharge is prohibited city-wide except listed exceptions; in this south area hunting is limited to deer on two of three December days (third Tuesday + following Wed/Thu, 8:30-13:00) or still-hunting deer with written landowner permits (max 6/day, access via private gate road off South St or Amber St); north of the line legal hunting is allowed with landowner permission (shotgun, pistol or <=.22 rifle, 150 yd from buildings/school/park lines). Doubts: the app's city outline is generalized (Census 1:500k), so edges are approximate; land west of Armory Dr's western terminus is assigned by straight extension of the road.

text: It shall be unlawful for any person to fire or discharge any pistol, rifle, shotgun, or any other firearms within the Gloucester Point sanitary district, including any and all weapons which propel a projectile by pneumatic means, as pellet guns or B-B guns, unless said firearm is being fired or discharged while a person is protecting life or property.
method: Gloucester Point Sanitary District polygon taken from Gloucester County GIS "Special Tax Districts" layer (feature SPTXDTDSCRP = 'Gloucester Point Sanitary District'), queried with outSR=4326&f=geojson; clipped to the app county outline, simplified 0.0001°, rounded to 5 decimals.
notes: Area ≈ 686 acres, 0.43% of the county. The polygon is published by county GIS staff but only inside a 2020 sanitary-district analysis web map (no standalone authoritative layer was found; the county GIS server maps.gloucesterva.info was unreachable). It could not be checked against the 1967 plat (Plat Book 4 p.35) and 1973 enlargement cited in the ordinance's editor's note. Shape matches the Gloucester Point peninsula south of the Hayes area, bounded by the York River and Sarah Creek. ~4 acres along the southern shore fall outside the app's generalized county outline and were clipped.

text: It shall be unlawful to shoot or discharge any firearms, including any and all weapons which propel a projectile by pneumatic means, as pellet guns or B-B guns, except for the protection of one's life or property, in the following described area of the county: Commencing at State Route 1301 and the mean high water mark of Timberneck Creek at a public landing commonly called "Field's Landing," thence running in an easterly direction along the center of State Route 1301 to U.S. Route 17, thence running in a southerly direction along the center of U.S. Route 17 to Gloucester Point sanitary district, thence in a westerly direction along the Gloucester Point sanitary district line to the mean high water mark of York River, thence along the mean high water mark of York River in a northwesterly direction to the mouth of Timberneck Creek, thence in a northerly direction along the mean high water mark of Timberneck Creek to the point of beginning.
method: Constructed from the legal description: land (county outline minus TIGER 2023 area water, i.e. York River and Timberneck Creek, approximating the mean high water mark) was split by TIGER 2023 lines for State Route 1301 (Fields Landing Rd, extended ~180 m west to meet Timberneck Creek), U.S. Route 17 (George Washington Memorial Hwy) and the Gloucester Point Sanitary District boundary (county Special Tax Districts layer); the face bounded by Fields Landing Rd (north), US 17 (east), the sanitary district line (south), and the York River / Timberneck Creek shore (west) was kept.
notes: Area ≈ 1862 acres, 1.17% of the county. TIGER confirms SR 1301 = Fields Landing Rd, running from Timberneck Creek east to US 17. The road/water legs are reliable (TIGER shoreline approximates mean high water; US 17 is a divided highway so the line is a carriageway, not the exact center, ~10-20 m). The southern edge inherits the sanitary district polygon's uncertainty (see the gloucester-point-sanitary-district manifest). Applies to pneumatic guns too.

text: Locust Lane Subdivision and the adjoining R-2 zoning district in Midway Acres Subdivision, more fully described in an exhibit filed with a copy of the ordinance from which this section derives in the office of the county administrator.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. Script: scratchpad scripts/proc.py. Union of (a) all tax parcels in tax-map blocks 60A-2 through 60A-7 (the platted lot strip along Locust Lane, legal descriptions 'LOCUST LANE ...' and 'MIDWAY L..'), and (b) the R-2 zoning polygon (OBJECTID 59) in block 60A-12 next to Midway Acres lots L1-L3; closing of 15 m to include the Locust Lane roadway; holes < 3000 m2 filled; tolerance 0.00002 deg.
notes: Result 0.19 km2 (~47 acres), 0.05% of the county, near Midway/US-33 west of Stanardsville around 38.24 N, -78.383 W. The ordinance's exhibit was not available, so the boundary is reconstructed from parcel legal descriptions. The lots along Locust Lane are a single numbered sequence (lots 4-53, sections 1-4); lots 13-14 and 18-53 are described 'LOCUST LANE (ADD)', while lots 4-11 and 15-17 and lettered lots A-E at the southwest end are described 'MIDWAY'. All of them were included as the Locust Lane subdivision (this may overstate it by ~10 small lots at the southwest end). The 'adjoining R-2 zoning district in Midway Acres' was taken to be the only R-2 polygon in the area: block 60A-12, which also holds 'MIDWAY ACRES L1-L3'. Today those Locust Lane lots are zoned A-1 in the parcel records. Also note exception (b)(2): discharge on private property with the owner's permission, with reasonable care to keep projectiles on the property, is not a violation.

text: upon, from or across any land located within the boundaries of any residential or industrial district as so classified and defined by chapter 24 or any commercial district.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. Script: scratchpad scripts/proc.py. Zoning district polygons dissolved; morphological closing of 10 m; holes < 2000 m2 and parts < 200 m2 dropped; tolerance 0.0001 deg.
notes: Result 311.9 km2 = 49.4% of the county (eastern Henrico/Varina is largely A-1, so it is less than 'most of the county'). Henrico's C-1 is the Conservation district, not commercial, so it is excluded. Judgment calls: office districts (O-1..O-3, O/S) were treated as commercial; mixed-use/planned districts (UMU, SMX, CMU) contain residential and commercial uses and were included. Interstate/major-road ROW appears unzoned or A-1 in the data and is left out (discharge on/across roads is prohibited anyway by the same section). Not represented: the section's separate bans on public land/public places/streets; the deer exemption (13-59(b): >=5 ac zoned agricultural; 13-61(d): >=2 ac agricultural for bows) only applies in agricultural zoning, which is outside this polygon. Conditional suffix 'C' and labels with '*' are the same base districts.

text: It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge any firearms or pneumatic gun in the county ... in or within 50 feet of the boundaries of any recorded subdivision ... Recorded subdivision. a. Any subdivision of property into two or more lots (i) which occurred after August 31, 1964; (ii) has a plat recorded in the county's circuit court clerk's office; and (iii) where the new lots created are to be used for residential or commercial purposes. b. The following subdivisions divided prior to August 31, 1964, as shown on the map titled James City County Pre-August 1964 Subdivisions Prohibited from Discharging Firearms, dated September 20, 2011: [57 named subdivisions] c. Any subdivision where two thirds of the lot owners have petitioned the board of supervisors to be included ... d. Recorded subdivision shall not include property divided pursuant to family subdivision, condemnation, or other board of supervisors' approved subdivision of property.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. Script: scratchpad scripts/proc.py. Subdivision polygons unioned, then buffered outward 50 ft (15.24 m); holes < 2000 m2 filled, parts < 100 m2 dropped; tolerance 0.00003 deg (~3 m) to keep the 15 m buffer edge accurate.
notes: Result 130.3 km2 = 32% of the county (incl. buffer). The county layer is a named-subdivision/neighborhood inventory; it does NOT necessarily include every small post-1964 recorded subdivision (e.g. 2-5 lot divisions along rural roads), and petitioned subdivisions (c) cannot be identified, so the true prohibited area is LARGER than this polygon. Of the 57 pre-1964 subdivisions named in (b), about 48 match layer names (some by variant spelling, e.g. Canterbury Hills, Sadie Lee Taylor, Schulyer and Troy Smith, Belen and Carriage Heights Parker, Lakewood for Marl Hills; 'Tom and Hazel Kearney' may be Thomas & Hattie Kearney). I could not find D. Warren Marston, Dandridge Davenport & Piggott, Frank Anderson, James Wesley Jones (Estate), Levi & Lettie Wallace, Rado Banks, Signor Bradby, Washington Jones (Estate) or Yearda Lee Smith, and the 2011 pre-1964 map was not found online. Some layer entries (e.g. Busch Gardens, Eastern State Hospital, JCC Riverfront Park campground, airport) may not meet the legal definition but were kept, which is the cautious choice. Not modeled: the 300 ft dwelling/commercial building/animal shelter rule, the 800 ft Colonial Heritage dwelling rule, and the 'ammunition crossing such areas' clause.

text: The area within a line following State Route 620 (Braddock Road) from the boundary with Fairfax County west to its intersection with State Route 659, then along State Route 659 north to its terminus at State Route 7, then following State Route 7 west to the corporate limits of the Town of Leesburg, then following the corporate limit line of the Town of Leesburg north and west to the Potomac River, then east along the Potomac River boundary with Maryland to the Fairfax County line, then southwest along the Fairfax County line to its intersection with State Route 620.
method: official layer
notes: Official county polygon; its west edge follows Rte 659, south edge Braddock Rd (Rte 620), north edge Rte 7 to the Leesburg town limits then the Potomac, matching TIGER 2023 lines within a few tens of meters. Clipped to the app's generalized county outline (lost 0.4% of the official polygon area, mostly along the Potomac/Fairfax edges). The layer dates from 2019; the Leesburg corporate-limit segment reflects the town limits at that time. Inside this area firearms discharge is prohibited except the hunting uses in 684.03(a)(2) (deer with handguns, shotguns or muzzleloaders using a single projectile; other hunting with .22 rimfire or smaller rifles, handguns, shotguns, muzzleloaders). Note a separate county service FIREARMS_PROHIBITED_POLY (services1.arcgis.com/MxjRokvPm7bjslyR, edited 2026) models the remaining lawful-discharge area county-wide net of 100-yd building/park/school and 50-yd road buffers; it was not used because it mixes in the buffer rules, but its eastern edge is consistent with this polygon.

text: (a) It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge, hunt or attempt to hunt with any gun, or to hunt or attempt to hunt any game animal or game bird with a firearm, or other weapon except bows, in the Merrifield Acres Subdivision, including lands immediately adjacent to such subdivision which are owned and under the control of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. Hunting within the Merrifield Acres Subdivision using bows is not prohibited hereby.
method: Subdivision: the "Merifield Acres" polygon (OBJECTID 1248, FIPS 51117, 1,205 ac) from the Southside Planning District Commission regional GIS subdivision layer, unioned with the 677 assessor tax parcels (Mecklenburg County parcel layer hosted by Southside PDC) whose interior point falls inside it (assessor subdivision code 287 "ROANOKE POINT"; ten legal descriptions say "MERIFIELD"). Adjacent USACE land: no USACE fee-boundary layer for Kerr Lake was found (PAD-US 4.1 fee layers have none here), so it is approximated as non-water land (TIGER 2023 area water) with no tax parcel within 120 m of the subdivision polygon, kept only where touching it. Simplified 0.0001 deg, rounded to 5 decimals.
notes: Ordinance spells "Merrifield"; local data and street names use "Merifield". The subdivision feature is high confidence (regional GIS subdivision polygon agrees with assessor lots; only ~2.4 ha of lots stick out). The USACE feature is a low-confidence approximation: Corps land around Kerr Lake typically runs from the lot lines to the shoreline (largely already inside the PDC polygon, which follows the shoreline) and the actual Corps tract extent beyond 120 m is not mapped. Bow hunting is not prohibited by this section (firearms/other weapons only). The county outline used by the app is coarse; geometry was not clipped to it.

text: It shall be unlawful to shoot or discharge any firearm in the following described area of the county: Piankatank Shores Subdivision. All those certain lots or parcels of land lying along each side and at the end of State Route 690, shown on Tax Map 37A, and recorded within the deed books of the circuit court clerk's office of the county, at the following pages: Section A-Book 80, page 294; Section B-Book 81, page 290; Section C-Book 81, page 301; Section D-Book 84, page 83; Section E-Book 85, page 442; Section G-Book 86, page 166; Section H-Book 86, page 171.
method: Downloaded all Middlesex County tax parcels (county ArcGIS Online layer taxparcels_cama). Selected every parcel whose TaxMapNo begins with 37A (the tax map named in the ordinance; legal descriptions read "P SHORES LOT n SEC A..H"), plus parcel 37-42C described as "PIANKATANK SHORES LOTS". Unioned, 25 m morphological closing to absorb internal roads, holes < 2 ha filled, clipped to county outline, simplified 0.0001 deg, rounded to 5 decimals.
notes: 643 parcels. Every section named in the ordinance (A,B,C,D,E,G,H) is found in the assessor legal descriptions on Tax Map 37A blocks 1-8. Parcel-derived outline; road rights-of-way between lots are approximated by the closing step. The adjacent Piankatank Golf & Country Club lots (map 37 block 15) are NOT included.

text: It shall be lawful to trap and hunt, with shotgun using shotgun shells, wildlife, as defined in Code of Virginia, tit. 29.1, except freshwater fish, in those areas of the city zoned agricultural; except that it shall not be lawful to hunt or attempt to hunt in such areas on or within 100 yards of any public highway or public street.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. Script: scratchpad scripts/proc.py. District polygons dissolved; parts < 100 m2 dropped, holes < 1000 m2 filled; tolerance 0.00005 deg.
notes: This is the area where shotgun hunting is ALLOWED (everywhere else in the city discharge is prohibited by 74-208). Result 9.6 km2 = 16% of the city. The city's sources disagree: assessor parcels coded A cover 5.6 km2 (95% within this output); the draft-map '86 Base' layer 10.8 km2; a 2023 UVA copy 6.6 km2. The official viewer layer used here is mostly a superset of the assessor parcels, so some edges may be over-generous for an 'allowed' area; hunters should confirm a parcel's zoning with Petersburg Planning. About 3 km2 of this polygon lies inside Petersburg National Battlefield (NPS), where hunting is not allowed regardless of zoning. The 100-yard setback from public highways/streets in 74-209 is NOT applied to this polygon and must be applied separately. Shotgun with shotgun shells only.

text:
Sec. 26-17: "...it shall be unlawful for any person willfully to shoot or discharge any firearm within or into any of the shooting-prohibited areas of Stafford County, designated as such in section 26-18, following." Sec. 26-18(a): (1) Lake Arrowhead: Beginning at the intersection of Garrisonville Road (State Route 610) and Lake Arrowhead Drive; thence southerly along Lake Arrowhead Drive to its intersection with Hillcrest Drive; thence southerly along Hillcrest Drive to its intersection with Van Horn Lane; thence easterly along Van Horn Lane to its intersection with Forest Drive; thence southerly along Forest Drive to Beech Drive; thence westerly along Beech Drive to its intersection with Boundry Drive; thence westerly along Boundry Drive to its intersection with Lake View Drive; thence northeasterly along Lake View Drive to its intersection with Arrowhead Drive. This zone includes all roads which are interior to Lake Arrowhead Subdivision.
(2) Garrisonville: Beginning at the intersection of Austin Run and I-95; thence northerly along I-95 to Aquia Creek; thence westerly along Aquia Creek to its intersection with Joshua Road (State Route 643); thence southerly along Joshua Road to its intersection with Garrisonville Road (State Route 610); thence westerly along Garrisonville Road to its intersection with Joshua Road; thence southerly along Joshua Road to its intersection with Saint George's Drive; thence southwesterly along Saint George's Drive crossing an unnamed creek to Choptank Road; thence southerly along Choptank Road to Mountain View Road (State Route 627); thence southeasterly along Mountain View Road to Shelton Shop Road (State Route 648); thence northeasterly to Winding Creek Road (State Route 628); thence southeasterly along Winding Creek Road to Austin Run; thence easterly along Austin Run to I-95.
(3) Aquia: Beginning at I-95 and Aquia Creek; thence easterly along Aquia Creek to its intersection with Jefferson Davis Highway (U.S. Route 1); thence northeasterly along Jefferson Davis Highway to its intersection with Telegraph Road (S.R. 637); thence northeasterly along Telegraph Road until its intersection with an unnamed tributary to Aquia Creek; thence easterly along unnamed tributary to its intersection with a straight line extending in a northwesterly direction from Bosun Cove; then southeasterly along said line and Bosun Cove until its intersection with Harpoon Drive; thence southeasterly along Harpoon Drive to Beacon Cove; thence southerly along Beacon Cove back to its intersection with Harpoon Drive; thence southerly along Harpoon Drive to its intersection with Lighthouse Cove and Bulkhead Cove back to their intersection with Harpoon Drive; thence southwesterly along Harpoon Drive to its intersection with Titanic Drive; thence southeasterly along Titanic Drive to Aquia Creek; thence easterly along Aquia Creek to the RF&P Railroad track; thence southeasterly along the RF&P Railroad track to Courthouse Road (S.R. 630); thence westerly along Courthouse Road to I-95; thence northerly along I-95 to Aquia Creek. This shooting-prohibited area includes all roads interior to Aquia Harbour Subdivision.
(4) South Stafford: Beginning at I-95 and Warrenton Road (State Route 17); thence easterly along Warrenton Road to Musselman Road; thence southerly along Musselman Road to Steely Lane; thence easterly along Steely Lane to Old Forge Drive; thence northerly along Old Forge Drive to Warrenton Road; thence easterly along Warrenton Road to its intersection with Lendall Lane; thence southerly along Lendall Lane to its intersection with Ingleside Drive; thence westerly and easterly along Ingleside Drive; thence easterly along Ingleside Drive to its intersection with Washington Street; thence easterly along Washington Street to River Road; thence easterly along River Road to Kings Highway (State Route 3); thence easterly along Kings Highway to Leonard Street; thence southerly along Leonard Street to Mimosa Street; thence easterly along Mimosa Street to Rumford Road; thence northerly along Rumford Road to Kings Highway; thence easterly along Kings Highway to a stream leading from Lake Carroll; thence northerly along said stream to Lake Shore Drive; thence northerly along Lake Shore Drive to Carroll Circle; thence easterly from Carroll Circle to Ashbury Drive (inclusive of all the streets within Briarwood Estates Subdivision); thence easterly along Ashbury Drive to its intersection with Colebrook Road (State Route 682); thence westerly along Colebrook Road to its intersection with Ferry Road (State Route 606); thence westerly along the south side of Ferry Road to its intersection with Braddock Drive; thence northerly along Braddock Drive to Claiborne Run; thence northeasterly along Claiborne Run to its intersection with Town and Country Drive; thence northerly along Town and Country Drive to its intersection with White Oak Road (State Route 218); thence easterly along White Oak Road to Kendallwood Drive; thence northerly along Kendallwood Drive to its intersection with Karen Terrace; thence westerly along Karen Terrace to its intersection with Sebastian Road; thence northerly and southerly along Sebastian Road (all inclusive of Sebastian Road) to its intersection with Matthew Lane; thence easterly along Matthew Lane to its intersection with Kendallwood Drive; thence southerly along Kendallwood Drive to its intersection with White Oak Road; thence westerly along White Oak Road to its intersection with Little Whim Road (State Route 669); thence northerly along Little Whim Road to its intersection with Roger Street; thence westerly along Roger Street to its intersection with Edwards Drive; thence northerly along Edwards Drive to its intersection with Deacon Road; thence westerly along Deacon Road to its intersection with Leeland Road (State Route 626); thence northerly along Leeland Road to its intersection with Morton Road (State Route 624); thence westerly along Morton Road to its intersection with Forbes Street (State Route 627); thence southerly along Forbes Street to its intersection with Manning Drive (State Route 1005); thence westerly along Manning Drive to its intersection with Jefferson Davis Highway (U.S. Route 1); thence southerly along Jefferson Davis Highway to Warrenton Road; thence westerly along Warrenton Road to its intersection with I-95.
(5) Widewater: Beginning at Aquia Creek and the RF&P Railway; thence northeasterly along the RF&P Railway to railroad Mile Marker 73; thence in an easterly direction to the Potomac River; thence south along the bank of the Potomac River to Brent Point; thence westerly along the bank of the Potomac River to Simms Point; thence north and northwesterly along the bank of Aquia Creek to the RF&P Railway.
method: Official Stafford County GIS layer "shooting_prohibited_areas" (owner gis_stafford_va, described as "in accordance with Sec. 26-18 of the Stafford County Code"), all 5 features, queried with outSR=4326&f=geojson; one feature per ZONE_NAME kept as the "name" property; clipped to the app jurisdiction outline, simplified 0.0001°, rounded to 5 decimals. Visually checked against the §26-18 descriptions (relative positions of Lake Arrowhead, Garrisonville, Aquia/Aquia Harbour, Widewater peninsula east of the RF&P railroad, South Stafford/Falmouth area).
notes: Combined share of county: 11.6% (Lake Arrowhead 0.19%, Garrisonville 3.7%, Aquia 4.1%, South Stafford 2.5%, Widewater 1.1%). The county layer appears parcel-based (fields count parcels per zone), so edges follow parcel lines rather than road centerlines. ~69 acres of the Widewater zone along the Potomac fall outside the app's generalized county outline and were clipped away. §26-18(b)/(c) allow the Board to add contiguous or new areas after a public hearing; the GIS layer (2022) may lag or lead the DWR-published text. Separate county-wide rules also apply (no shooting within 100 yd of occupied structures without written permission, within 100 yd of private roads in subdivisions with lots of 10 acres or less, no hunting within 100 yd of primary/secondary highways).

text: No person shall hunt with firearms or other weapons in the Surry Landing on the James subdivision, including future and developed lots, as recorded in the subdivision plat in Deed Book 120 Pages 785-793, and as amended by Plat Book 7, Page 267 in 2010 and as further amended by Plat Book 8, Page 23 in 2011.
method: Queried the Surry County public parcel layer (CivQuest-hosted county GIS) around Surry Landing Drive. Every parcel with legal description "LOT n SURRY LANDING (SUB.)" carries tax-map PIN 14-3-*; their recorded plat references (PLAT-120-785, PLAT-7-267, PLAT-8-23, PLAT-11-55) match the plats cited in the ordinance. Selected all 10 parcels 14-3-1 ... 14-3-9 and 14-3-1A (lots 1-10), unioned with a 15 m closing to absorb the internal road, simplified 0.0001 deg, rounded to 5 decimals.
notes: All ten parcels whose legal description names Surry Landing are on one tax-map block (14-3) and cite the ordinance's plats. Lot 1 (14-3-1, ~89.5 ac, PLAT-8-23 of 2011) is a large residual tract that holds the "future" lots; it is included because the ordinance expressly covers future lots and the 2011 plat amendment. Parcel lines are from county GIS and may differ slightly from the recorded plat; shoreline edge follows the parcel polygons.

text: north or west of the trace of the line beginning at the intersection of North Landing Road and the Chesapeake-Virginia Beach city boundary line; thence northwardly along North Landing Road to Indian River Road; thence eastwardly along Indian River Road to New Bridge Road; thence northeastwardly along New Bridge Road to Sandbridge Road, thence eastwardly along Sandbridge Road to its intersection with the Atlantic Ocean, or across any land north of False Cape State Park and east of Shipps Bay and Point Creek.
method: constructed from official City of Virginia Beach street centerlines + TIGER 2023 water
notes: Main area: city outline split by the trace line (North Landing Rd from the North Landing River bridge north to Indian River Rd, Indian River Rd east to New Bridge Rd, New Bridge Rd NE to Sandbridge Rd, Sandbridge Rd east to the ocean), path traced along city centerlines; north/west side kept, including water (ordinance says 'land or water'). The trace line itself is high confidence. Second clause ('land north of False Cape State Park and east of Shipps Bay and Point Creek'): no feature named 'Point Creek' exists in GNIS/TIGER for Virginia Beach; interpreted as Hell Point Creek, the gut that separates the Sandbridge peninsula from the mainland marsh just south of Sandbridge Rd. Built as the barrier-beach land (water removed) east of Hell Point Creek, North Bay, Shipps Bay and Sand Bay, from Sandbridge Rd south to the north edge of False Cape State Park (~36.6305 N); includes Sandbridge Beach and the Back Bay NWR beach strip. Marsh islands west of Sand Bay (inside Back Bay) were NOT included - ambiguous whether they are 'east of Shipps Bay'. Back Bay NWR is federal land with its own hunting rules. Outline is the app's generalized city boundary, so edges along the Chesapeake line and the coast are approximate. Not shown: the separate (a)(1) Elbow Rd/Salem Rd/Landstown/Princess Anne line (only affects small-tract shotgun permits) and the (d) 150-yard rule, which applies citywide.

text: Except as hereinafter provided, all hunting with firearms or other weapons, including bow and arrow, is prohibited in the following designated subdivisions or other areas of the County which, in the opinion of the Board of Supervisors, are so heavily populated as to make such hunting dangerous to the inhabitants thereof. There shall be erected appropriate signs where they may reasonably be seen, designating the boundaries of said subdivisions and areas in which hunting is prohibited. However, this chapter shall not prohibit hunting by bow and arrow by a property owner on such owner's own property in such subdivision, provided that such hunting is done at least 100 yards from residences and roads. A. Within the boundary lines of Skyland Estates Subdivision, as shown on Warren County Tax Map 23A Sheets 1 through 6. B. Within the boundary lines of Apple Mountain Lake Subdivision as shown on Warren County Tax Map 22B. C. Within the boundary lines of all sections of Shenandoah Farms Subdivision and those adjacent parcels as shown on the following Warren County Tax Maps: 7A; 7A1; 15B; 15C; 15D, Sheets 1 and 2; 15E, Sheets 1 through 5; 15F; 15G; 15H; 23C, Sheets 1 through 9; and 24C. D. Within the boundary lines of all sections of Shenandoah Shores Subdivision as shown on Warren County Tax Map 13C, Sheets 1 and 2. E. Within or from the South Fork of the Shenandoah River from the upstream edge of the State Route 619 bridge to the confluence of the South Fork of the Shenandoah River with the North Fork of the Shenandoah River. F. Within the boundary lines of all sections of Lake Front Royal Subdivision as shown on Warren County Tax Map 39C. G. Within the boundary lines of all sections of Apple Mountain Lake South Subdivision as shown on Warren County Tax Map 31C. H. Within the boundary lines of all sections of High Knob Subdivision as shown on Warren County Tax Maps 31B and 31B1. I. Within the boundary lines of all sections of Stonewall Estates Subdivision as shown on Warren County Tax Map 11G.
method: Downloaded all 27,646 Warren County parcels from the county GIS (WarrenGISUpdates/Parcels, which carries tax map "map"+"ins" and a "subdivision" name field). For each lettered item, selected every parcel on the tax map(s) cited in the ordinance (e.g. 23A, 22B, 15E) plus any parcel whose subdivision field names that subdivision; unioned, 30 m morphological closing to absorb internal roads, holes < 5 ha filled, simplified 0.0001 deg, rounded to 5 decimals. Item E (river segment): TIGER 2023 area-water polygon "South Fork Shenandoah Riv" for Warren County, cut at the TIGER "State Rte 619" crossing, keeping the downstream piece to where TIGER switches to North Fork / Shenandoah River polygons (the confluence at Riverton). Cross-checked against Census 2023 CDPs: 95-100% of each subdivision polygon falls inside the same-named CDP (CDPs are larger).
notes: Subdivision items A-D, F-I are parcel-derived from the exact tax maps cited by the ordinance and agree with the county subdivision-name field; boundaries are lot-line unions so road rights-of-way/edges are approximated. Item C deliberately includes all parcels on the cited maps ("and those adjacent parcels") — including Linden Heights on 23C. Apple Mountain Lake West (22C) is NOT cited and not included. Item E is medium confidence: it relies on TIGER naming the road "State Rte 619" at the crossing near 38.904N -78.214W (south edge of Front Royal) and on TIGER water polygons; about 58% of that river segment lies within the Census boundary of the Town of Front Royal. The river feature has ordinance_item "E". Bow hunting by an owner on own property >=100 yd from residences/roads is excepted (not mapped).
